1.explanation:
• src/ol/renderer/webgl/TileLayer.js: At line 338 this file uses layer.getMinZoom() directly when computing a tile grid index for WebGL tile rendering, causing mismatches between view zoom and tile grid levels.
• src/ol/renderer/canvas/TileLayer.js: The Canvas renderer contains a similar code path that also uses getMinZoom() as a tile grid zoom index and would suffer from the same missing‐tile issue.
• src/ol/layer/Layer.js: This file shows the correct pattern (lines 415–423) using view.getResolutionForZoom or tileGrid.getZForResolution in conjunction with getMinZoom()/getMaxResolution. It serves as the reference implementation for fixing the renderer logic by replacing the direct getMinZoom() usage with a resolution‐to‐z lookup.
1.bug_scenario:
In the WebGL (and similarly the Canvas) TileLayer renderers, layer.getMinZoom() is being used directly as a tile grid zoom index when fetching and rendering tiles. Because getMinZoom() returns a view‐centric zoom level (not a tile‐grid index), supplying it directly to the tile grid can result in no tiles being requested or rendered when the view’s zoom range doesn’t align with the source tile grid’s levels—e.g.
a source with zoom levels 0–3 in a map view that spans 0–18 will end up sending z=3 (minZoom) instead of the grid index for the current resolution, so tiles at other zooms never load.

2.explanation: Both the WebGL and Canvas TileLayer renderers use layer.getMinZoom() directly when determining which tile grid Z to request. getMinZoom() returns a view zoom (unrelated to grid Z), so treating it as a tile index leads to skipped tile loads. These two files must be edited to remove or replace layer.getMinZoom() with the correct conversion (e.g. tileGrid.getZForResolution(layer.getMaxResolution()) or view.getResolutionForZoom(layer.getMinZoom())).
2.bug_scenario: When rendering a TileLayer, the WebGL (and by symmetry the Canvas) renderer is incorrectly using layer.getMinZoom() as if it were a tile-grid zoom index. Since layer.getMinZoom() returns a view zoom level, not a tile grid Z, tiles whose view zoom doesn’t match the grid are never requested or rendered — resulting in missing tiles when the map view’s minZoom differs from the source’s tileGrid levels.
